findings.title: Retry cleanup is not scoped to SMS reminders
findings.body: The new delete predicate is `(SMS reminder whose date has passed) OR (retryCount > 1)`. The retry-count branch has no `method: SMS` condition, so this SMS cron endpoint will delete future EMAIL or WHATSAPP workflow reminders whenever their `retryCount` exceeds one. Keep the method restriction outside the OR (or repeat it in the retry branch) so retry cleanup cannot silently remove unrelated workflow notifications.

findings.title: Reminders with no usable recipient never reach the retry limit
findings.body: `retryCount` is only incremented after entering the `message?.length && sendTo` branch. An SMS attendee reminder for a booking without `smsReminderNumber`, an SMS-number step without `sendTo`, or a reminder that renders an empty message remains `scheduled: false` with `retryCount: 0`. It will therefore be selected by every cron run until its scheduled date instead of being discarded after the configured attempts. Treat an absent destination or message as a failed, terminal, or retryable scheduling outcome.

findings.title: Retry increments lose attempts when cron executions overlap
findings.body: The count is read by `findMany` and later written back as `reminder.retryCount + 1` (also in the catch block at line 195). Concurrent cron invocations can both read `0`, both fail, and both write `1`, so two failures are recorded as one and the reminder is attempted more than the intended two times. Use an atomic database increment and, ideally, atomically claim the unscheduled reminder before calling Twilio so overlapping jobs cannot process the same row.
